description.plain:
Adaptive Damage: This effect deals either physical or magic damage depending on whether you have more bonus attack damage or ability power.
* Greater bonus attack damage → Physical damage
* Greater ability power → Magic damage
If the damage contribution of AD and AP are zero or otherwise equal, the damage type depends on the champion's adaptive type.
Gain 1 gold for each nearby minion killed by an ally (1400 range).

description2.plain:
Gain Gold gold when hitting an enemy champion with a basic attack or an ability that applies on-hit effects. This has a 5 second per-target cooldown.
* Melee Champions: 10 gold
* Ranged Champions: 3 gold

description.plain: A blink refers to a form of movement whereby a unit displaces from point A to B without traversing the space between.

A unit afflicted with Brittle has their Tenacity reduced by 30%.
Brittle's duration ends prematurely if the affected unit becomes immobilized or silenced.

description2.plain:
Tenacity (or Crowd Control Reduction) is a stat that reduces the duration of all incoming crowd control effects except displacements, drowsy, nearsight, stasis, and suppression.

If tenacity is reduced below 0, the crowd control duration increases.

description.plain:
Centered range is calculated from the center of a source unit's hitbox to the center of a target unit's hitbox.
* Centered range is used for most unit-targeted abilities.
* It is less effective and may seem to have diminished reach against large units.
A unit that is cleansed has all applicable crowd control status effects removed.

description2.plain:
* Due to the nature of the cleanse interaction, cleansing abilities and effects remain castable in circumstances that would otherwise inhibit casting, unless special-cased.
* "Cleanse" does not always refer to the act of removing all crowd control effects, some sources would specify only one or a few types of crowd control.
* A cleanse does not remove Stasis, but will remove the disable portion of Airborne.

description.plain: Critical strike refers to an effect that deals increased damage under specific circumstances, denoted as critical strike damage. The most common form of critical strike occurs on basic attacks, which triggers based on critical strike chance.

description2.plain: By default, a critical strike deals 200% of the normal damage. Critical damage modifiers such as Infinity Edge can increase this percentage.

description.plain: A unit that is disabled is affected by a status effect that prevents certain actions – such as movement, attacking, casting and/or seeing–blocked, reduced or controlled.
A dash is a quick movement action by a unit in which they move to a specific direction or location while traversing the intervening distance, ignoring the boundaries of terrain.

description2.plain:
The game engine does not take into account the height of the unit; dashes that depict air travel are considered to be on the ground for targeting purposes such as skill-shots.
* Dashes should not be confused with displacement effects, which are usually sourced from enemy units (and are classified as crowd control debuffs).
* Dashes are interrupted by stasis (from an enemy), knockdown, and blinks.
* Dashes are overridden by all move blocks, which includes displacements and other dashes, as well as a few other cases.
* Not all dashes can traverse terrain (e.g. Justice Punch, Searing Charge, Tumble).
* Some dashes gain increased distance when directed through terrain (e.g. Umbral Dash, Perfect Execution, Phantom Undertow).

description.plain: A dispel removes debuffs (e.g. - poison). It is distinct from Cleanse, which only removes crowd control, and Death, which removes all status effects (regardless of being positive or detrimental) that do not persist through death.

description2.plain:
Currently, the only sources of dispel exist in resurrection:
* Rebirth
* Cultivation of War
* Cell Division
* Chronoshift
* Guardian Angel

description.plain: Drain, better known as Vamp, is a term for various healing effects that are based on damage dealt, but are not spell vamp or life steal. Drain effects benefit from Heal and Shield Power.
A unit that is drowsy is slowed, and afterwards will fall asleep.

description2.plain: Removing drowsy or being displacement immune or immune to crowd control at its end will prevent sleep from occurring.

interrupts.plain: Does not interrupt any actions.

reduction.plain: The duration is unaffected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses.

description.plain:
Edge range is calculated from the edge of a source unit's hitbox to the edge of a target unit's hitbox.
* Edge range is mostly used for basic attacks; skill shots; and point-blank areas of effect (including auras).
* These become more effective against large champions, as the source gains more reach against them. This may be favorable or unfavorable: durable champions tend to be larger and thus easier to hit, and frail champions tend to be smaller and more difficult to hit.
Energized is an effect of certain items and runes that grants Charges, up to 100. Champions with Energized gain 6 Charges per basic attack and 1 Charge for every 24 units travelled by any means.

description2.plain:
At 100 charges, they become fully Energized, empowering their next basic attack to consume the charges on-hit to trigger bonus effects. All sources of Energized stack with each other:
* Rapid Firecannon grants bonus attack range and deals bonus damage.
* Statikk Shiv deals bonus damage and bounces to additional nearby targets.
* Stormrazor deals bonus damage and grants bonus movement speed.
* Voltaic Cyclosword deals bonus damage and grants Lethality.
* Fleet Footwork grants bonus movement speed and heals the user.

description.plain: A unit that is ghosted ignores unit collision, allowing them to move through other units and other units to move through them.
Grievous Wounds is a debuff that reduces self-healing, incoming healing, and health regeneration by 40%.

description2.plain: Grievous Wounds does not stack, the duration of the debuff will overlap on separate effects and refresh on the same effect.

description.plain:
Interrupt is a quality of crowd control that interrupts an in-progress effect, preventing its completion or causing the effect to go off at an interrupted state.

The following crowd control effects interrupt channeled and charged abilities (unless otherwise noted by the ability):
* Airborne
* Forced action (Charm, Flee, Taunt)
* Silence (Disrupt, Polymorph)
* Sleep
* Stasis
* Stun (Suspension)
* Suppression

The following crowd control effects interrupt dashes:
* Airborne
* Knockdown
* Stasis

Basic attack windups are interrupted by all forms of crowd control that inhibit attacking. Ground and Root only interrupt channeled and charged movement abilities.
A unit that is Invulnerable reduces all damage taken to 0 and prevents effects that trigger from damage.

A lunge refers to the movement of a champion during an ability's cast animation (such as short-ranged abilities) or an empowered attack's animation (such as empowerments that grant bonus range), in order to place the champion in range for a follow-up attack.

description2.plain: Lunge is a movement distinct from dashes, primarily by not triggering effects that would otherwise interact with dashes, such as Steadfast Presence and Doom 'n Gloom. Some lunges can traverse thin, player-generated terrain.

description.plain: Poison is the buff type for few select debuffs. Twin Fang has additional effects if it is cast on a poisoned target.

description2.plain:
The following inflict poison:
* Noxious Blast and Miasma
* Poison Trail
* Toxic Shot and Noxious Trap
* Deadly Venom

description.plain: A unit that is protected by Resurrection will enter a revival state and dispel most debuffs upon taking fatal damage. After the state completes, the unit is revived. Resurrection effects do not count for kills or assists.

description2.plain:
Resurrection sources have a hierarchy, and will trigger in the following order:
# Chronoshift
# Cultivation of War
# Guardian Angel
# Rebirth and Cell Division

Resurrection will always take precedence over zombie state effects. Entering resurrection does not cancel cast times. Bailout always takes priority over resurrection.

description.plain:
A spell shield refers to one of several effects that have the capacity to negate hostile abilities from applying to the recipient. A spell shield may negate many active effects coming from champion abilities, epic monsters, champion summoned units, and items, but almost none from runes and summoner spells with the only exceptions of Arcane Comet, Unleashed Smite, and Primal Smite which will be blocked.
* See the article for more details.
Takedown refers to a kill or assist being acceptable, with the type of enemy specified in each use case.

description2.plain: Takedown is associated with triggering a passive effect, or timed effects shortly after scoring.

description.plain:
Tenacity (or Crowd Control Reduction) is a stat that reduces the duration of all incoming crowd control effects except displacements, drowsy, nearsight, stasis, and suppression.

If tenacity is reduced below 0, the crowd control duration increases.

description2.plain:
* Tenacity stacks multiplicatively or additively based on the combination of effects.
* The duration of a crowd control debuff is calculated when it is applied, and tenacity can reduce it to a minimum 0.5 seconds.

description.plain: A unit that is untargetable is an invalid target; it can neither be selected nor hit by most effects. Effects that have already been applied are not invalidated by the unit becoming untargetable, unless they are special-cased to do so.

description2.plain: Becoming untargetable will interrupt acqusition. This also causes non-champions to lose aggro. Many untargetabilities additionally destroy all incoming unit-targeted projectiles.

description.plain: In addition to granting untargetability, vanish briefly hides a unit from the game's renderer, which causes it to become completely undetectable and invisible even to effects such as Oracle Lens. Vanished units are not indicated to be visible on the mini map. Vanished units are unable to act. As with all untargetability, tethers will still persist on a target that vanishes.

description2.plain: Vanish is not considered stealth and does not interact with sight effects.

description.plain: Sight is a property of units, structures, certain summoner spells, items, and abilities that represents a team possessing vision of a target area or unit. It is always center range. A line of vision cannot extend beyond terrain or an unrevealed brush.

description2.plain:
Sight can also refer to an effect that makes a unit visible regardless of the fog of war or brush, allowing them to be targeted. Standard sight cannot see stealthed units, but True Sight can.
* Nearsight is a crowd control debuff that inhibits sight; allied vision is lost in addition to a reduced sight radius.
* Obscured vision is similar to sight in a way that it can observe units, but does not render units targetable, rather it exposes their position and informs of their presence.
* Unobstructed vision is a form of sight that allows a unit to be able to see their full vision radius, ignoring any obstructions that would otherwise restrict visibility.
* All effects that use unit-targeting require sight of the target. Delayed unit-targeted attacks and spells can cancel if sight of the selected target is suddenly lost.

description.plain: True Sight reveals units through Fog of War, brush, and stealth. It does not bypass nearsight effects.
Exposed units are visible regardless of being in a Brush.
A ward that has been disabled does not grant sight. A disabled ward that is being attacked reveals the attacker briefly.

description2.plain: Control Wards and Effigies cannot have their sight disabled.

description.plain:
Ward Rubble forms whenever a ward is killed, times out, or is replaced, indicating the recent presence of a ward. An indicator displays above the rubble, that fades over time. Rubble and its indicator remain for 5 minutes.

The indicator has three stages, based on minutes passed after the rubble forms. It fades once at minute 1, and it fades again at minute 3, before permanently being removed from the map at minute 5.

Grants sight over the surrounding 900 units. Cannot have its sight disabled. Its sight also:
* Reveals and disables enemy wards.
* Reveals enemy stealthed traps.
* Reveals Camouflaged champions. 
It is also exposed to enemies while it is revealing one of the above stealthed units, or granting vision of a Tentacle.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain: Grants sight over the surrounding 500 units. Untargetable to allies.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain: Grants sight over the surrounding 1100 units.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain: Grants sight over the surrounding 900 units.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain:
A Sweeper Drone is a device that sweeps the surrounding area, granting obscured vision of enemy units within that are not visible. 
* Stealthed wards and traps are revealed. Stealthed wards are also disabled, lingering for 2 seconds after no longer being revealed.
* Each type of unit detected has a different colored silhouette.
** Champions are red.
** Non-champions are dark purple.
** Wards are light blue.
Grants sight over the surrounding 900 units.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain: Grants sight over the surrounding 900 units. Untargetable to allies.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain: Grants sight over the surrounding 450 units. Cannot have its sight disabled. Is untargetable and will be scared away if an enemy champion comes near it.

description2.plain: ⟦ward table⟧

description.plain:
Camouflage is a form of stealth that renders a unit hidden from enemy vision for a long period of time.
* Camouflaged units become visible while an enemy champion is inside their detection radius and they are within said enemy's line of sight (e.g. camouflaged unit is not already hidden by being inside a brush, enemy's line of sight is not obstructed by terrain or reduced below the detection radius by nearsight); when within the line of sight of an enemy Control Ward (900 units); or after being revealed by effects that apply True Sight.
* While a camouflaged unit is visible, they will see an exclamation mark above their health bar, warning them that they can be seen.

description2.plain: A stealthed unit's character model briefly shimmers for every instance of damage taken while stealthed. This shimmering does not make the unit selectable nor remove the stealth effect, only compromises its position.

description.plain:
Invisibility is a form of stealth that renders a unit hidden from enemy vision for a short period of time.
* Invisible units become visible only when affected by True Sight.

description2.plain: A stealthed unit's character model briefly shimmers for every instance of damage taken while stealthed. This shimmering does not make the unit selectable nor remove the stealth effect, only compromises its position.

description.plain: Stealthed traps are units that enter stealth shortly after being summoned, last for a duration, and are untargetable until they are revealed. They may be revealed and made targetable once again by Control Wards, Sweeper Drones (e.g. from A Harmless Scarecrow and Oracle Lens), and Umbral Glaive Blackout.
The Ancient Krug, Krug, and Mini Krug are neutral monsters on Summoner's Rift.

description2.plain: The Krug camp consists of one large Ancient Krug and one medium Krug that divide into a number of lesser Mini Krugs when slain. Killing the Ancient Krug spawns four Mini Krugs, and killing the Krug spawns two Mini Krugs, for a total of 8 units in the Krug camp. Killing this camp awards gold gold and experience.

description.plain: The Greater Murk Wolf and Murk Wolf are neutral monsters on Summoner's Rift.

description2.plain: The Murk Wolf camp consists of one large Greater Murk Wolf and two lesser Murk Wolves. Killing this camp awards gold gold and experience.

description.plain: The Crimson Raptor and Raptor are neutral monsters on Summoner's Rift.

description2.plain: The Raptor camp consists of one large Crimson Raptor and five lesser Raptors. Killing this camp awards gold gold and experience.

description.plain: The Golem camp consists of one large Golem and one lesser Golem. Killing this camp awards Gold gold and Experience.
The Wraith camp consists of one large Wraith and two lesser Wraiths. Killing this camp awards Gold gold and Experience.
The Wolf camp consists of one large Wolf and two lesser Wolves. Killing this camp awards Gold gold and Experience.

Monsters lose patience over time: while outside of their leash range; if they are unable to find their target (e.g. due to untargetability or stealth); and for non-epic monsters, each time they switch targets.

description2.plain: When patience drops to zero, the monster starts to walk back to its neutral position, healing itself and ignoring aggression, for up to 6 seconds. Attacking the monster in this state while it is inside its leash range will replenish some patience. If that timer runs out however, the monster will run back to the camp and heal rapidly, causing it to fully reset.

description.plain: Forced Action is a collective term used to refer to the crowd control types Berserk, Charm, Flee and Taunt.

description2.plain: A unit affected by Forced Action is forced to perform an action which is also no longer in their control, as well as has certain actions disabled. Forced Action effects cannot force the unit to perform an action that is disabled. These crowd control effects have the same reduction and resist interactions. Charm, Flee, and Taunt have the same removal interactions and also include a Source of the effect, which is the unit that casted the spell which applied the status effect. Forced Action effects are immobilizing effects.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts all channeled and charged abilities.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses or when the Source dies.

description.plain:
Immobilized units cannot control their movement, becoming unable to input movement commands and use movement spells. The following crowd control effects immobilize the unit: 
* Airborne
* Forced Action (Berserk, Charm, Flee, Taunt)
* Root
* Sleep
* Stasis
* Stun (Suspension)
* Suppression

Impaired movement is a similar term that, in addition to the above, also refers to units that are slowed.

A unit that is knocked airborne undergoes a forced displacement in a specified direction, to a specific point, or for a set duration at its current location, during which it is also unable to control its movement, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash. Airborne is an immobilizing effect.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups), and all channeled and charged abilities. The accompanying displacement overrides all other previous displacements, including dashes and other airborne effects.

reduction.plain: The duration of airborne and its forced movement execution time is unaffected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity, displacement immunity, and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: The forced movement that is applied alongside airborne effects cannot be removed by cleanses, which innately disables attacking and moving and can be overridden by dashing, blinking or lunging. Cleansing effects, with the exceptions of Breath of Life, Cleanse, Mikael's Blessing, and Quicksilver, remove the airborne status effect.

description.plain: A unit that is blinded will miss their basic attacks for the duration, comparable to attacking a target that is able to dodge or block, but not mechanically similar. Missed basic attacks will fail to deal damage and apply on-hit effects, with the exception of some empowered basic attacks. Blind does not prevent the unit from declaring attacks, unlike Disarm.

interrupts.plain: Does not interrupt any actions, but will prevent on-hit effects from being triggered by basic attacks.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses with the exception of Mikael's Blessing.

description.plain: A unit that is charmed is forced to move directly toward the Source (the unit that casted the Charm spell) for the duration, during which they're unable to perform issued movement commands, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash. All charms also apply a slow. Charm is an immobilizing effect. Forced action effects cannot force the unit to perform an action that is disabled.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities, as well as overrides previous Forced Action effects.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses or when the Source dies.

description.plain: A unit that is crippled has their total attack speed reduced by a percentage for the duration.

description2.plain: Sources of cripple stack multiplicatively with each other.

description3.plain: Negative cripple values will increase the unit's attack speed instead.

interrupts.plain: Does not interrupt any actions.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and cripple immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses and specifically Highlander.

description.plain: A unit that is disarmed is unable to declare basic attack commands for the duration.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts basic attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and Inferno Trigger.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses with the exception of Mikael's Blessing.

description.plain: When a unit is disrupted, it has their channeled and charged abilities interrupted.

description2.plain: Disrupt is not, and does not apply, a status effect. It should not be confused with Silence.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts all channeled and charged abilities, as well as abilities that would be interrupted by cast-inhibiting crowd control.

reduction.plain: The effect is instantaneous. There is nothing to reduce.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and effects that would otherwise resist Silence.

removal.plain: The effect is instantaneous. There is nothing to remove.

description.plain:
A unit that is entangled is rooted.

A unit that is rooted is unable to control its movement or activate movement spells for the duration. This effect does not innately knockdown a target that is already performing a dash. Rooted units can still be displaced. Root is an immobilizing effect.

description2.plain: Entangle is the signature effect of R, which also knock downs and disarms the targets.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and movement channels unless otherwise stated.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses. Mikael's Crucible will only remove the root portion of Entangle and not the disarm.

description.plain: A unit that is fleeing or feared is forced to move directly away from the Source (the unit that casted the Fear spell) for the duration, during which they're unable to perform issued movement commands, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash. All fears also apply a slow. Flee is an immobilizing effect. Forced action effects cannot force the unit to perform an action that is disabled.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities, as well as overrides previous Forced Action effects.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses or when the Source dies.

description.plain: A unit that is grounded is unable to activate movement spells for the duration. This effect does not innately knockdown a target that is already performing a dash. Grounded units can still be displaced.

description2.plain: Movement spells include all dash and blink abilities - including Recall / Empowered Recall and the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Dash, plus a number of additional cases. Ground is the only type of crowd control that is most commonly found in persistent area of effects, which will reapply the status effect continuously.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts movement channels unless otherwise stated.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses.

description.plain: Knockdown only affects units that are performing a dash or being displaced by an airborne effect. A unit that is knocked down has its dash or displacement interrupted and is placed on the ground instantly.

description2.plain: Knockdown is not a status effect.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts all dashes and airborne effects (displacement and status effects). Knock ups may have their airborne status removed on a case by case basis (inconsistent between sources), but their displacement always ends prematurely.

reduction.plain: The effect is instantaneous. There is nothing to reduce.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and displacement immunity.

removal.plain: The effect is instantaneous. There is nothing to remove.

description.plain: A unit that is nearsighted has their sight radius reduced and cannot see beyond their sight radius.

description2.plain: While nearsighted, units cannot reveal stealthed wards or traps. Nearsighted units lose vision of all their allies as well as all external sources of vision (including from wards or abilities). This prevents unit-targeted effects, including basic attacks, from being used outside of the unit's reduced sight radius. True sight and unobstructed vision do not bypass the vision blocked by nearsight. Sources of nearsight do not stack with each other; only the application with the greatest sight reduction will take effect.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts target commands if the nearsighted unit's target is outside of their new vision area and prevents automatic target acquisition.

reduction.plain: The duration is unaffected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity with the exceptions of Riposte and Black Shield.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses with the exceptions of Cleanse and Mikael's Blessing.

description.plain: A unit that is pacified is unable to declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash and Teleport. Pacify combines the effects of Disarm and Silence, with Polymorph also turning the target into a helpless critter.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities, as well as Glacial Storm.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses. Mikael's Crucible will only remove the silence portion of Pacify and not disarm.

description.plain:
A unit that is polymorphed is silenced and turned into a helpless critter. Polymorphed units are not indicated to be visible on the mini map.

A unit that is silenced is unable to cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash for the duration.

description2.plain: Polymorph combines silence with additional effects; it is the signature effect of Whimsy, which also disarms and reduces the target's movement speed for the duration.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts all attack windups (including uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses.

description.plain: A unit that is rooted is unable to control its movement or activate movement spells for the duration. This effect does not innately knockdown a target that is already performing a dash. Rooted units can still be displaced. Root is an immobilizing effect.

description2.plain: Moving includes movement commands. Movement spells include all dash and blink abilities - including Recall / Empowered Recall and the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Dash, plus a number of additional cases.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts movement channels unless otherwise stated.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses.

description.plain: A unit that is silenced is unable to cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash for the duration.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts all channeled and charged abilities.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses.

description.plain: A unit that is asleep is unable to control its movement, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash for the duration. Sleep occurs after the duration of drowsiness finishes. Sleep is an immobilizing effect.

interrupts.plain: Falling asleep interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable basic attacks) and all channeled and charged abilities.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity, displacement immunity, and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses and taking damage that is not persistent nor indirect. Damage originating from minions, and small and medium monsters, will not affect sleep. Any damage instance less than or equal to a value of 10 post-mitigation is also ignored and will not affect sleep.

description.plain: A unit that is slowed has reduced movement speed for the duration. Slows based on a percentage value cannot reduce a target below 110 movement speed. Some slows will instead modify the target's movement speed to a static value, which may not be further reduced nor increased.

description2.plain: Only the slow with the highest value is taken into movement speed calculations. All additional slows are ignored until the higher-valued slow wears off. The strength of slows may amplify or decay over their duration. Slows of the same debuff cannot stack and will instead refresh on each application unless otherwise stated.

description3.plain: Negative slow values will increase the unit's movement speed instead.

interrupts.plain: Does not interrupt any actions.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.The strength is reduced by slow resist.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and slow immunity.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses, Decisive Strike, Highlander and Biggest Snowball Ever!.

description.plain: A unit that is in stasis is unable to control its movement, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use any summoner spells for the duration, while also being invulnerable and untargetable. Stasis is an immobilizing effect.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups), all channeled and charged abilities and all dashes and displacements. Units that are being knocked up will be placed on the ground, but aren't knocked down (the airborne status is not removed in this case).

reduction.plain: The duration is unaffected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity, displacement immunity, and Goes Where He Pleases. Epic monsters and turrets are special cased to be affected by stasis despite them being crowd control immune.

removal.plain: Cannot be removed by any means (except through death), and will prevent the activation of abilities that would usually remove crowd control effects. Quicksilver will either be placed on a short cooldown, remain usable, or become disabled.

description.plain: A unit that is stunned is unable to control its movement, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash for the duration. Stun is an immobilizing effect.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses.

description.plain: A unit that is suppressed is unable to control its movement, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use any summoner spells for the duration. Animations for suppression abilities vary and so must not be confused with airborne effects. Suppression is an immobilizing effect.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities.

reduction.plain: The duration is unaffected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses with the exceptions of Cleanse and Mikael's Blessing.

description.plain: A unit that is suspended is stunned for the duration. It also pretends to be airborne while the stun holds (Last Breath can be cast on a suspended enemy). A unit that is stunned is unable to control its movement, declare attacks, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash for the duration. Suspension is an immobilizing effect.

description2.plain:
Unlike common stuns, suspension is prevented by effects that prevent displacements and becoming suspended also interrupts the ongoing movement of dashes and airborne effects.

Like common stuns, it is affected by Tenacity and can be fully removed by cleansing effects.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups) and all channeled and charged abilities and all dashes and airborne effects (displacement and status effects). Knock ups will not have their airborne status removed if there is no sourced debuff, but their forced movement still ends.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity, displacement immunity, and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Fully removed by Cleanses.

description.plain: A unit that is taunted will attempt to perform basic attacks on the Source (the unit that casted the Taunt spell) for the duration, during which they're unable to perform issued movement or attack commands, cast abilities, activate items or use the summoner spells Flash, Teleport, Hexflash, and Mark / Dash. Taunt is an immobilizing effect. Forced action effects cannot force the unit to perform an action that is disabled.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts attack windups (excluding uncancellable windups and windups against the Source) and all channeled and charged abilities, as well as overrides previous Forced Action effects.

reduction.plain: The duration is affected by Tenacity.

resist.plain: Resisted by crowd control immunity and Goes Where He Pleases.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanses or when the Source dies.

description.plain: Within a drafted team, the Top Laner is the champion assigned to the top lane.
Within a drafted team, the Jungler is the champion assigned to the jungle. A Jungler needs to be able to clear jungle camps without too much difficulty and ambush other champions in lane.

Within a drafted team, the Support is one of the two champions assigned to the bottom lane alongside the Bottom Carry. This role's initial goal is to assist their more vulnerable team mate through the earliest stages of the game, and is a position that suits champions with either utility, disengage or high base damage.

description2.plain: Within a duo lane, the optimal strategy for earning gold is to designate a single champion to farm while the other is recommended to purchase an economy item. The Support is expected to fulfill the latter designation: consequently, the position is not suitable for champions that are highly dependent on item-based power spikes. The Support is also expected to be the primary contributor to the team's vision.

description.plain: Within a drafted team, the Mid Laner is the champion assigned to the mid lane.

Within a drafted team, the Bottom Carry is one of the two champions assigned to the bottom lane alongside the Support. Being the most vulnerable, the Bottom Carry has to acquire as much gold as possible to purchase key items that will greatly increase their fighting potential.

description2.plain: Within a duo lane, the optimal strategy for earning gold is to designate a single champion to farm while the other is recommended to purchase an economy item. The Bottom Carry is expected to fulfill the former designation: the position is made for champions that highly depend on item-based power spikes.

description.plain: Fill refers to being assigned to any lane in order to complete a drafted team. On Summoner's Rift, that would be: Top, Jungle, Mid, Bot, Support.
Roamer is both a role that a champion can fulfill within the team and an unofficial position that a champion can be assigned to.

description2.plain:
* Roaming as a role is generally considered implicit of the Jungler, but it is also a strategy often adopted by Middle, Top and Support players, especially those using Catcher or Assassin champions. 
* Roaming as a position usually comes at the expense of the Support or Jungler, whereby the player performs the above role exclusively without laning. Roaming as a position is common at very low levels prior to unlocking the Smite summoner spell (as an alternative to duo-Top), but can also be employed at other tiers of play as well as during featured game modes, such as Hexakill.

description.plain: Melee champions have a basic attack range usually within 200 units. A melee attack does not use a projectile to deal damage, therefore not subject to effects that mitigate projectiles, like Wind Wall. Some champions can shift between a ranged and melee form, and certain items/runes differ for melee characters.

Ranged champions have a basic attack range usually beyond 300 units. Many deal damage through projectiles, which are subject to mitigating effects like Wind Wall. Some champions can shift between a ranged and melee form, and certain items/runes differ for ranged characters.

Mana (also known as MP) is a stat that is the resource of many champions necessary to cast most of their abilities. Mana can be restored via mana regeneration and some abilities, items, runes, and buffs. Mana is represented in-game by the blue bar within the HUD, indicating the champion's current mana and maximum mana. Current mana is reduced by expenditure through paying an ability's mana cost.

A champion that is manaless does not use nor benefit from mana or mana regeneration, and includes the following:
* Energy users
* Flow users
* Fury users
* Heat users
* Health exclusive users
* Resourceless users
⟦:energy⟧

description2.plain: Energy has a maximum of 200 (except for Shen, with 400), and regenerates rapidly, at a rate of 10 energy per second. This means that energy champions are not at risk of depleting their resource over a long period of time, however the small capacity restricts the rapid usage of multiple spells.

description.plain: Heat is a gating mechanic unique to Junkyard Titan that is intended to limit up-time but, like Energy, does not have an indefinite down-time. Heat is not required to cast abilities and is instead generated on-ability-cast, with Overheating preventing users from performing certain actions for a set time.

Fury is an umbrella term for many named resources that must be generated before being usable, compared to Mana or Energy that exist in some quantity beforehand. For most users, this resource is only required by a single ability or passive effect. It represents momentum and encourages sustained aggression from users, often gating a power-spike or empowerment. Fury generation varies between users, but is always generated in-combat (e.g. on-hit, ability casts or taking damage) and often decays when out of combat.
;Known as:

* Reign of AngerFury
* Rage
* Battle Fury
* Dragon Fury
* Crimson Rush
* Courage
* Grit
*

Flow is a resource that must be generated before being usable, compared to Mana that exists in some quantity beforehand. It is represented beneath the health bar that is blue until filled, and then white. Unlike Fury and its variants, however, Flow is not affected by the unit's combat status. With only one example of Flow, the validity of this exception may be called into question in the future.
Healing replenishes a unit's current health, but never above their maximum health.

A shield adds hitpoints over the unit's health that absorbs the next instances of damage in place of actual health. This can be improved by various items and effects depending on the type of shielding.

On-hit effects refers to a category of effects that are applied on some damage instances, through the TriggerOnHitEvents property. Champion basic damage through their basic attack applies on-hit effects by default, but many other spells are made to do the same. The damage of most on-hit effects itself is in turn usually tagged proc, which is non-reactive (= does not trigger further damage-tag-specific effects).

description2.plain:
Some important clarifications:
* A critical strike is not an on-hit effect. Their application is handled completely separately.
* Health restoration from life steal is not an on-hit effect. However, damage can be made to apply life steal through the ApplyLifesteal property, and this is also employed on some on-hit effects.

description.plain:
Magic damage is one of the three damage types.
* Applies:
** Bloodletter's Curse Vile Decay (conditionally)
** Morellonomicon and Oblivion Orb Grievous Wounds
** Omnivamp
* Triggers:
** Hexdrinker and Maw of Malmortius Lifeline
* Mitigated by:
** Magic resistance
** Damage shields & Magic shields
** Invulnerability
** Damage reduction
** Death's Dance Ignore Pain

Physical damage is one of the three damage types.
* Applies:
** Black Cleaver Carve
** Chempunk Chainsword, Executioner's Calling and Mortal Reminder Grievous Wounds
** Omnivamp
** Physical vamp
* Triggers:
** Armored Advance Noxian Endurance
* Mitigated by:
** Armor
** Damage shields & Physical shields
** Invulnerability
** Damage reduction
** Death's Dance Ignore Pain

True damage is one of the three damage types.
* Applies:
** Omnivamp
* Mitigated by: 
** Damage shields
** Invulnerability

A unit that is phased ignores terrain collision, allowing them to move through terrain and structures. Additionally, they have unobstructed vision while inside terrain.
* Phasing units can move up to 550 units beyond the outer-edge of the battlefield.
* Enemy units cannot see phasing units while inside of terrain unless they have terrain-piercing vision (e.g.: Heightened Senses, Hawkshot or Comet of Legend).
** Enemies will be notified if nearby terrain is infested if a phasing unit is within 1000 units - with an indicator being placed on the terrain with a direct line between the phased and the enemy champion. Slightly less than standard sight radius, but more than the camouflage detection radius.
* While moving inside terrain, phasing units are considered to be dashing, so knockdown effects would stop them from moving.
** Immobilizing crowd control will interrupt phasing abilities prematurely.
* While in terrain, phasing units will not be considered unseen for the sake of Duskblade of Draktharr.
* Phasing unit's sight radius is not extended beyond merged terrain while nearsighted.
A unit that is Purged has their buffs and positive status effects removed with the exception of shields.

description2.plain:
Purge is classified as a debuff and not a type of crowd control, and consequently cannot be reduced or removed except with the use of revival effects. This is with the notable exceptions of:
* Riposte, which classifies it as an immobilizing crowd control effect.
* Black Shield, which will prevent the application of purge.
Other forms of crowd control immunity will not prevent the purge debuff being applied.

description.plain: A unit that is Wilted is unable to restore health through any means (Incoming heals and self-heals, life steal, spell vamp and draining effects) and activate healing abilities.

interrupts.plain: Interrupts all healing abilities, including Drain, Infinite Duress, Meditate and Monsoon.

reduction.plain: The duration is reduced by tenacity, which stacks multiplicatively.

resist.plain: Resisted by unstoppable units, Black Shield, Ragnarok, Riposte and Void Shift.

removal.plain: Removed by Cleanse, Quicksilver, Mikael's Crucible, Battle Roar, Ragnarok, Remove Scurvy and Unbreakable Will.

description.plain: Crowd control immunity prevents any type of crowd control from being applied to the unit. CC which has already been applied will still have an effect on the unit. Epic monsters (excluding a summoned Rift Herald) and turrets are always immune to all crowd control, with the exception of stasis.
Slow resist is a stat that directly reduces the effectiveness of slows.
Slow immunity is a status effect that prevents the application of slows.

description2.plain:
The following prevent the application of slows:
* Sentry
* H-28G Evolution Turret
* Highlander
* Biggest Snowball Ever!
* Fury of the North
* Ixtal's Impact
* Total crowd control immunity

description.plain: Unit-targeted is a targeting paradigm which requires a valid target within range to cast on. The target needs to be visible in order to use the effect. All basic attacks use unit-targeting.

A projectile or missile is any entity not classified as a unit (champion, minion, monster, etc.) that travels at any given velocity.
* Moving units are not considered projectiles under any circumstance (including dashing units, airborne units, or units thrown by some abilities such as Force of Will or Roar of the Slayer.).
* Unbreakable, Rebuttal, Blade Whirl, and Wind Wall can block, destroy and / or stop projectiles.
** Some ranged basic attacks (including turrets) and abilities don't use projectiles and will bypass projectile-blocking effects.
* Some abilities will destroy all currently incoming homing projectiles.

Destroying or popping of a projectile references an effect that destroys all homing missiles currently targeting a specific unit, such as ranged projectile-based basic attacks. Destroyed missiles will do the same thing as if they were destroyed by Wind Wall or Blade Whirl (usually vanishing without any effect).

description2.plain:
The following abilities perform one or more projectile popping events:
* Most abilities and effects that grant untargetability pop projectiles when the unit gains the status effect.
** Alpha Strike in particular pops targeted projectiles on each game tick for its duration.
** Hallowed Mist pops all projectiles (from enemy champions outside of its area of effect) targeted at her that attempt to pass through or be inside its area of effect.
* Upon entering or leaving Realm of Death.
* Upon successfully completing the channel of:
** Stand United
** Gate
** Teleport

description.plain:
Stealth conceals a unit from enemies' view and prevents them from selecting it, and grants ghosting while not seen. Stealth allows one to avoid and ambush enemies or re-position in a fight.
* There are three categories of stealth, based on the conditions necessary to gain sight of the user: Camouflage, Invisibility, and stealthed traps. True sight invariably reveals stealthed units.
* Certain actions may break stealth, such as starting an attack, casting an ability, using certain item actives, and others.
* A stealthed unit's character model briefly shimmers for every instance of damage taken while stealthed. This shimmering does not make the unit selectable nor remove the effect, it only compromises the unit's position.

description2.plain: Stealth is not a form of untargetability; units can still be hit by effects that do not require sight of targets, such as auto-targeted, direction-targeted (skillshots) and location-targeted effects.

description.plain:
A channeled ability is an ability that can be prevented from reaching its conclusion, by the user themself and / or because of other effects.

A charged ability has a channel that is toggled by two activations - the first begins the charging and the second will fire the ability. While using Quick cast, the player must keep the hotkey held down to charge the ability and release to fire. Unlike normal channels, the caster is still able to move freely and cast movement abilities, unless otherwise stated.

A movement channel is a type of channel which also involves the caster moving from their position, usually in the form of traversal such as dashes and blinks. This means the crowd control effects ground and root, which both inhibit the activation of movement spells, can interrupt the channel.

description2.plain:
The following crowd control effects will interrupt all channels (except uninterruptible ones):
* Airborne
* Forced action (Charm, Flee, Taunt)
* Silence (Disrupt, Polymorph)
* Sleep
* Stasis
* Stun (Suspension)
* Suppression

description.plain: A champion that is locked out is unable to perform certain actions such as casting abilities, moving, or attacking due to currently performing another action that must complete. The prevented actions can vary per instance.

description2.plain: Lockout does not interact with crowd control mechanics unless otherwise stated.

description.plain:
A unit that is affected by cast-inhibiting crowd control is unable to cast abilities, activate items, or use summoner spells. The following crowd control effects disable casting of all spells and abilities as well as interrupt all channels:
* Airborne
* Forced Action (Berserk, Charm, Flee, Taunt)
* Silence (Polymorph)
* Sleep
* Stasis
* Stun (Suspension)
* Suppression

description2.plain: Note that Disrupt is not a status effect and solely interrupts channels, and thus cannot fall under this classification. However, abilities that would be interrupted by forms of cast-inhibiting crowd control are also interruptible by Disrupt. Root and Ground only disable movement spells and abilities. Stasis and Suppression are the only crowd control effects that disable all summoner spells from use; all other cast-inhibiting crowd control only disable movement summoner spells.

description.plain: Executes deal damage equal to 100% of the target's current health, which is usually true damage, while ignoring all mitigations. Those that affect champions may additionally have the property of breaking 100% of the target's current shields before applying their damage.

description2.plain: Most executes do not ignore invulnerability, resurrection and effects that grant a minimum health threshold. If they do, they are termed raw damage.

description.plain: Omnivamp is a collective term used to refer to healing from dealing physical damage, magic damage, and true damage.

description2.plain: The healing from omnivamp is reduced to 33% effectiveness against minions and monsters with area, pet, and persistent damage.

description.plain: The basic attack (or "auto") is the default means by which a unit deals damage, usually equaling 100% AD physical damage. Basic attacks are normally unit-targeted edge range spells, and the attack range stat determines their reach.

description2.plain:
The caster must stand still to complete a brief windup before launching a basic attack. Depending on the caster:
* If a caster's attacks are non-projectile (e.g. melee) launching the attack deals damage immediately.
* If a caster's attacks are projectile, launching the attack sends a projectile that follows the target and deals damage upon striking them.
The caster then incurs a brief cooldown, based on their attack speed. Basic attacks' damage may trigger on-hit effects only upon dealing damage. On-attack effects will always trigger upon the attack's windup completing.

description.plain: Proc damage is a primary damage tag. Effects that should not interact with anything else are usually tagged Proc.

description2.plain: Generic interactions can still trigger from proc damage, such as minion aggression and healing from damage dealt via omnivamp or physical vamp (with the appropriate properties).
